text.p: JERUSALEM, Aug 18 - These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Security triad talks begin in Ramallah; government downplays report Mahaneh Yehudah bombing planned in England.
- Histadrut declares labour dispute.
- Caltex to buy into Dor energy.
- Barge carrying toxic waste sinks off Haifa.
HAARETZ
- Peak in number of work seekers: 145,000.
- Palestinian Authority cooperating in investigation of Jerusalem bombing.
- Teachers intend to disrupt opening of school year.
- Sharp 5.4 pct jump in money supply, Bank of Israel Governor expected to raise interest by 0.5 pct.
- Phillips president in Israel to weigh company's potential activities.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Tunisia pulling out its representative in Israel.
- Unemployment grows, slowdown sharpens.
- Prime Minister won't ease closure against security officials recommendations.
MAARIV
- Unemployment worsens, investment down, stocks fall, strikes threatened.
- Security apparatus wary of easing closure but prefers to free Palestinian funds.
GLOBES
- Positive surprise on stock exchange: only two pct drop despite Wall Street fall.
- Slump of 5.4 pct in money supply, chances of 0.5 interest hike grow.
